review_scope: Original references, Phase 1 masks/edges/overlays, Phase 2 component masks/overlays, and Phase 2.1 refined masks/overlays for all five views

front.phase1: Contours and edges capture the ring, stone, and prongs, but the silhouette includes lower cast-shadow regions.
front.phase2: Stone localization is correct but contains facet holes; prongs are fragmented; shadow includes underside regions.
front.phase2_1: Closed stone and four-prong topology are correct. Prong masks are coarse rounded regions and the stone boundary is an idealized ellipse.

side.phase1: Ring opening and setting edges are captured; the bottom floor shadow is included in the silhouette.
side.phase2: Stone is localized, but shank and setting are heavily merged and shadow traces reflective shank edges.
side.phase2_1: Shank and setting are disjoint, but their shoulder boundary is a geometry-driven hard cut rather than an observed semantic boundary.

top.phase1: Strong silhouette and edge extraction with lower shadow contamination similar to front view.
top.phase2: Stone is localized but perforated by highlights; prongs fragment into many regions.
top.phase2_1: Four-prong topology and closed stone are correct; boundaries remain idealized and coarse.

angled.phase1: Outer ring and setting are captured, with reflections and floor shadow affecting the lower contour.
angled.phase2: Shank and setting are strongly merged; stone and prong masks are fragmented.
angled.phase2_1: Structural separation improves, but the amodal stone is overly elliptical, prongs remain fragmented, and part of the shoulder is assigned to setting by a fixed region rule.

back.phase1: Ring opening and basket edges are captured; bottom shadow contaminates the silhouette.
back.phase2: Shank and setting merge; the single prong region represents an occluded aggregate rather than four instances.
back.phase2_1: Head and shank are structurally separated, but the cut is coarse and visible/hidden prong identity is unresolved.

blocking_findings: No human-verified component masks exist, so true IoU, Dice, and boundary F1 cannot be measured.
Phase 1 silhouettes include cast shadows in every view to varying degrees.
Phase 2.1 prong masks are topology-correct in front/top but not pixel-accurate.
The angled stone and side/back setting boundaries are geometry priors rather than fully observed boundaries.
Shadow masks still include reflective-metal edge responses.
recommended_next_gate: Create five human-reviewed gold masks, then refine with GrabCut/HQ-SAM and report IoU, boundary F1, component count, and cross-view consistency.
